title: Pay Per Call Communities, Forums and Events
h1: Pay per call communities, forums and events worth joining
description: Where pay per call publishers, affiliates and buyers meet: forums, LinkedIn groups and industry events, plus how to use them without spamming.
faq: Is there a pay per call community for beginners?

Yes. Affiliate marketing forums such as affLIFT have dedicated pay per call sections where beginners ask about networks, offers and tracking, and LinkedIn groups for media buyers regularly share pay per call opportunities.
Where do pay per call buyers and publishers meet?
Online, mostly on LinkedIn and in affiliate forums. In person, at lead generation and affiliate conferences such as LeadsCon and Affiliate Grand Slam.
How do I find buyers in a community without spamming?
Answer questions, share what you have learned and only mention what you offer when it solves the problem someone posted. Read each community's rules on promotion first.
body:
The best pay per call communities are the places where publishers, affiliates and buyers already talk every week: affiliate marketing forums with pay per call sections, LinkedIn groups for media buyers and lead generators, and industry conferences. Joining them helps you learn which verticals and networks are working, find buyers and publishers, and spot problems before they cost you money.

Online forums

affLIFT

affLIFT is an affiliate marketing forum with a dedicated pay per call section and a separate tracking section. Members discuss networks, home-service and insurance offers, number leasing and campaign setup, and many threads come from people just getting started.

AffiliateFix

AffiliateFix is a long-running affiliate forum where pay per call threads cover trackers, call costs and which networks to try. Older threads are still useful for understanding the basics.

LinkedIn

LinkedIn has become one of the busiest places for pay per call business. Buyers post when they need more calls in a vertical, networks post when they want new publishers, and publishers post the verticals they can deliver. Useful habits:

  • Search posts for phrases such as "buying inbound calls", "publishers needed" or your vertical plus "pay per call", sorted by latest.
  • Join groups for affiliate marketers and media buyers, where call buying and selling posts appear daily.
  • Reply with specifics: the verticals, states and hours you can cover, not a generic pitch.

Industry events

Lead generation and affiliate conferences bring buyers, networks, publishers and platforms into one place. LeadsCon focuses on lead generation and performance marketing, and Affiliate Grand Slam brings together affiliates, networks and advertisers, with pay per call companies among the exhibitors. Book meetings before you travel and bring a one-page summary of your traffic or buying needs.

How to get value from a community

  1. Read before you post. Learn the rules on self-promotion and the questions that come up again and again.
  2. Answer one question a week. Helpful answers build a reputation faster than any pitch.
  3. Share real lessons. What happened when you tested a vertical, a routing rule or a new traffic source.
  4. Move serious conversations to a call. Agree rules, caps and payouts in writing before sending traffic.

Turning connections into campaigns

Once a community introduction turns into a deal, you need the basics in place: a tracking number per source, routing rules that respect the buyer's hours, caps and states, and payouts each partner can check.
